import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/training_4.csv"
]

# Target schema columns
target_columns = ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']

# Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file in source_files:
    # Read CSV with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
    df = pd.read_csv(file, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema (all sources have same schema)
    df = df[target_columns]
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the exact same schema as the target,
# we can simply concatenate (union) all source DataFrames
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure data types are string for all columns as per target schema
for col in target_columns:
    target_df[col] = target_df[col].astype(str)

# Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
